result.builder:
Goal: one pull request on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test that adds a new workspace `packages/jsonl-lint` and meets every acceptance line of https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102. The repo currently has no `packages/` directory; the root `package.json` already declares `workspaces: ["packages/*"]` and its `test` script runs `npm test --workspaces --if-present`. CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) runs `npm ci` then `npm test` on Node 22.

Acceptance lines (each one must hold at the PR head):
1. "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none"
2. "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2"
3. "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]"
4. "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes"
5. "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool"
6. "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"

Steps:
1. Create `packages/jsonl-lint/package.json`: `"name": "jsonl-lint"`, `"type": "module"`, `"scripts": { "test": "node --test" }` (exactly `node --test`; node 22 discovers `test/*.test.js`), `"bin": { "jsonl-lint": "bin/jsonl-lint.js" }`, `"engines": { "node": ">=22" }`, `"private": true` is fine. No `dependencies` field (or an empty one); no devDependencies needed either.
2. Create `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` (plain ES module, zero dependencies) exporting a named function `lint(text)`. Split the text on `\n` (strip a trailing `\r` per line so CRLF files work). Line numbers are 1-based over the physical lines. Skip lines that are empty or whitespace-only. For every other line, `JSON.parse` it; on failure push `{ line, error }` where `error` is the parse error's message (a non-empty string). The last line is checked even if the text does not end in a newline (a torn/unterminated row like `{"x":` must be reported); a single trailing newline must not produce an extra empty row error. Return the array (empty when the text is clean).
3. Create `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang, executable (`chmod +x`, and make sure git records mode 100755). It takes one argument `<file>`. With no argument: print a usage message to stderr, exit 2. If the file cannot be read (missing, etc.): print an error to stderr, exit 2. Otherwise read it as UTF-8, call `lint`, and for each result print to stdout exactly `<file>:<line>: <error>` where `<file>` is the argument as given; exit 1 if there was at least one result, else exit 0 with no output. Import `lint` from `../src/index.js` via a path resolved relative to the bin file (`new URL('../src/index.js', import.meta.url)` or a relative import), so it works from any working directory.
4. Add `node:test` tests under `packages/jsonl-lint/test/` (e.g. `test/lint.test.js` and `test/cli.test.js`) using `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`. Cover, with clearly named tests: a clean file (lint returns `[]`; CLI exits 0, no stdout); a bad middle row (e.g. rows 1 and 3 valid, row 2 invalid → exactly one result with line 2); a torn last row with no trailing newline (reported with its line number); blank lines (blank and whitespace-only lines skipped, yet line numbers of later bad rows stay the physical 1-based numbers); and the exit codes 0, 1 and 2 (spawn the CLI with `child_process.spawnSync(process.execPath, [binPath, file])` on temp files written into `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), ...))`; check the `<file>:<line>: ` output format for exit 1; for exit 2 check both no argument and a missing file, and that stderr is non-empty). Resolve paths from `import.meta.url`, not from the cwd.
5. Write `packages/jsonl-lint/README.md`: what it does, usage `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file>`, output format, the exit codes (0 clean, 1 bad rows, 2 missing file/no argument), the `lint(text)` API returning `[{ line, error }]`, and how to run the tests.
6. Update the root `README.md`: under "What is here", replace the "No tools yet: `packages/` is empty..." bullet with a bullet listing `packages/jsonl-lint` (the literal text `jsonl-lint` must appear) and a one-line description.
7. Run `npm install` at the repo root so `package-lock.json` gains the new workspace (otherwise `npm ci` in CI fails because the lock is out of sync), and commit the updated `package-lock.json`. Then run `npm ci && npm test` from the repo root and confirm the jsonl-lint tests run and pass, and run the CLI by hand on a clean file, a file with a bad middle row and a torn last line, a missing file and no argument, checking output and exit codes.
8. Commit everything, push, and open exactly one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test. The PR body must contain the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102` (full URL, exactly as written). Do not open a second PR; push fixes to the same branch.
9. Wait for the `test` workflow to finish on the PR head commit and make sure it concludes success; if it fails, fix and push again until it is green at the head.
result.verifier:
Verify the pull request for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102. Check out the PR head commit and run every command from the repository root. Do one check per acceptance line, in this order, and report PASS or FAIL for each with the output that decided it.

Check 1. Expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none"
Run:
```
d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '{"a":1}\n\n{bad\n[1,2]\n{"x":' > "$d/t.jsonl" && node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/t.jsonl"; echo "exit=$?"
```
Then run:
```
d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '{"a":1}\n\n[2]\n' > "$d/ok.jsonl" && node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/ok.jsonl"; echo "exit=$?"
```
PASS if the first command prints exactly two error lines, one starting with `<that file path>:3: ` and one starting with `<that file path>:5: `, each followed by a non-empty error text, prints no line for rows 1, 2 (blank) or 4, and ends with `exit=1`; and the second command prints nothing before `exit=0`. FAIL if a line is missing (in particular line 5, the unterminated last line), an extra line appears (e.g. for the blank line 2 or a valid row), the line numbers are off, the format differs from `<file>:<line>: <error>`, or either exit code differs.

Check 2. Expect line: "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2"
Run:
```
d=$(mktemp -d) && node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js "$d/missing.jsonl" >"$d/out" 2>"$d/err"; echo "exit=$?"; echo "stdout:"; cat "$d/out"; echo "stderr:"; cat "$d/err"
```
and:
```
d=$(mktemp -d) && node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js >"$d/out" 2>"$d/err"; echo "exit=$?"; echo "stdout:"; cat "$d/out"; echo "stderr:"; cat "$d/err"
```
PASS if both show `exit=2` and a non-empty message under `stderr:`. FAIL if either exit code is not 2 or stderr is empty.

Check 3. Expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]"
Run:
```
node --input-type=module -e "import { lint } from './packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js'; console.log(JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n\n{bad\n[1]\n{\"x\":')), JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n[2]\n')))"
```
PASS if the import succeeds and the first printed value is an array of exactly two objects with `line` 3 and `line` 5 respectively, each having an `error` property (a string), and the second printed value is `[]`. FAIL if the import fails, `lint` is not a named export, the return is not an array of `{ line, error }` objects, or the lines differ.

Check 4. Expect line: "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes"
Run:
```
node -e "const p=require('./packages/jsonl-lint/package.json'); console.log(JSON.stringify({name:p.name,type:p.type,test:p.scripts&&p.scripts.test,dependencies:p.dependencies}))"
```
and:
```
ls packages/jsonl-lint packages/jsonl-lint/test; npm test -w packages/jsonl-lint; echo "exit=$?"
```
Then read the test files under `packages/jsonl-lint/` that the test run executed.
PASS if `name` is `jsonl-lint`, `type` is `module`, `test` is a script that runs `node --test`, `dependencies` is absent or empty; the workspace tests run under `node:test` and end with `exit=0`, with zero failures; and the test files import from `node:test` and contain tests covering each of: a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn (unterminated) last row, blank lines, and the CLI exit codes. FAIL if any of these fields differ, there are runtime dependencies, the tests fail or do not run, or any of the five named cases has no test.

Check 5. Expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool"
Run:
```
test -f packages/jsonl-lint/README.md; echo "readme=$?"; grep -n 'jsonl-lint' README.md; echo "grep=$?"
```
PASS if it prints `readme=0`, and `grep=0` with at least one matching line in the root `README.md` that lists the jsonl-lint tool. FAIL if `readme=1` or the root README does not mention the tool.

Check 6. Expect line: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run:
```
gh api "repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/pulls?state=all&per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select((.body // "") | contains("Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102")) | "\(.number) \(.state) \(.head.sha)"'; echo "exit=$?"
```
then:
```
sha=$(gh api "repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/pulls?state=all&per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select((.body // "") | contains("Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102")) | .head.sha' | head -n1) && echo "head=$sha" && gh api "repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/commits/$sha/check-runs" --jq '.check_runs[] | "\(.name) \(.status) \(.conclusion)"'; echo "exit=$?"
```
and, with the PR head checked out:
```
git rev-parse HEAD; npm ci && npm test; echo "exit=$?"
```
PASS if the first command lists exactly one PR (the one under review) whose body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102`; the check-runs for its head sha include the `test` workflow's job (`test`) with status `completed` and conclusion `success`; `git rev-parse HEAD` equals that head sha; and `npm ci && npm test` ends with `exit=0` with the jsonl-lint tests running and passing. FAIL if no PR or more than one PR matches, the body lacks that exact sentence, the test check is missing, pending or not successful at the head, the checked-out commit is not the head, or `npm ci`/`npm test` fails.

Advisory (not pass/fail conditions):
- Check that `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` is committed executable (`git ls-files -s packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` shows mode 100755) and has a node shebang.
- Check that `package-lock.json` includes the new workspace; an out-of-sync lock makes `npm ci` fail.
- Try running the CLI from another directory (e.g. `cd /tmp && node <repo>/packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file>`) and on a CRLF file to spot path or `\r` handling bugs; report findings as notes.
